articles.headline: Rwanda Plans Formula 1 Race as Part of Broader Development Strategy
articles.dek: The country aims to leverage the African Grand Prix, set to begin in the early 2030s, to boost tourism, attract investment, and foster economic growth.
articles.lead: Rwanda has announced a 10-year agreement to host the African Grand Prix, with a purpose-built circuit planned in Bugesera for the early 2030s. This initiative is presented not as an isolated event but as a component of a larger strategy for sports, tourism, entertainment, and innovation.
articles.takeaway: The country aims to leverage the African Grand Prix, set to begin in the early 2030s, to boost tourism, attract investment, and foster economic growth.
body: Rwanda has announced a 10-year agreement to host the African Grand Prix, with a purpose-built circuit planned in Bugesera for the early 2030s. This initiative is presented not as an isolated event but as a component of a larger strategy for sports, tourism, entertainment, and innovation.

The project is situated adjacent to a new international airport under construction and is designed for year-round utilization. The goals include facilitating skills transfer, stimulating local business growth, and establishing a continental motorsport hub. Formula 1 has framed the deal as a long-term partnership focused on tourism, investment, and human capital development.

This approach aligns with a development model that prioritizes catalytic infrastructure, visibility, and connectivity to drive economic multipliers. Rwanda's strategy echoes that of nations like Singapore and Gulf states, which have used significant infrastructure and major events to attract capital, talent, and technology.

Rwanda has a history of pursuing ambitious projects to signal its seriousness to investors, including transforming Kigali and focusing on services, ICT, and tourism. These efforts have contributed to sustained economic growth and increased foreign investment interest, positioning the country as a regional hub.

While acknowledging the importance of healthcare and education, the strategy posits that economic growth, fueled by initiatives like the Grand Prix, provides the necessary resources for increased social spending. The success of the project will ultimately be measured by factors such as attendance, tourism impact, local employment, and private capital attracted in the 2030s.

Masaka Views Eco Estate is being built in Masaka, a neighbourhood in Kigali’s Kicukiro District, near an area designated for healthcare facilities. Once completed, the development will comprise 382 housing units, including apartments, semi-detached family houses and townhouses.

articles.headline: Gahini School Reopens Visually Impaired Program
articles.dek: Groupe Scolaire Gahini in Rwanda has resumed its inclusive education program for students with visual impairments after a three-year hiatus, aiming to provide a model for mainstreaming these learners.
articles.lead: Groupe Scolaire Gahini has reopened its program for students with visual impairments, marking a return to inclusive secondary education at the Kayonza-based institution. The program, which had ceased admitting visually impaired learners three years ago, was a pioneer in integrating students with disabilities into mainstream education since the late 1990s.
articles.takeaway: Groupe Scolaire Gahini in Rwanda has resumed its inclusive education program for students with visual impairments after a three-year hiatus, aiming to provide a model for mainstreaming these learners.
body: Groupe Scolaire Gahini has reopened its program for students with visual impairments, marking a return to inclusive secondary education at the Kayonza-based institution. The program, which had ceased admitting visually impaired learners three years ago, was a pioneer in integrating students with disabilities into mainstream education since the late 1990s.

The Rwanda Union of the Blind (RUB) welcomed the reopening, emphasizing the importance of GS Gahini as the country's sole inclusive school for visually impaired students at the secondary level. RUB's executive director, Jacques Mugisha, stated that such an environment is crucial for developing social relationships, preparing for university, and improving employment prospects.

The school's headteacher, Luke Karemangingo, confirmed the resumption of the program, noting that stakeholders including the Ministry of Education and the Rwanda Basic Education Board (REB) agreed on its continuation. Karemangingo explained that the program's previous halt was due to a gradual decline in admission requests, with the last group of six students completing their studies in the 2024-2025 academic year.

Irenée Muyizere, director of special needs and inclusive education at REB, affirmed the school's commitment to inclusive education, highlighting GS Gahini's role as a model institution. The school has a dedicated resource room, Braille equipment, and trained staff to support visually impaired learners.

Six students were admitted to the program when the current academic year began in September. RUB plans to continue engaging with visually impaired students to encourage enrollment at GS Gahini, reinforcing the school's legacy of inclusive education.

articles.headline: Rwanda's Chief Justice Warns New Judges Against Poor Rulings Fueling Court Backlogs
articles.dek: Supreme Court President Domitilla Mukantaganzwa urges newly sworn-in judicial officials to prioritize accuracy and professionalism to prevent cases from being prolonged and exacerbating existing judicial burdens.
articles.lead: Rwanda's Supreme Court President, Domitilla Mukantaganzwa, has cautioned newly appointed judicial officials that incorrect rulings can worsen the country's court backlogs. Speaking after a swearing-in ceremony for seven judges and eight court registrars, Mukantaganzwa emphasized that flawed decisions do not resolve disputes but instead lead to further litigation, thereby increasing the workload on the judiciary.
articles.takeaway: Supreme Court President Domitilla Mukantaganzwa urges newly sworn-in judicial officials to prioritize accuracy and professionalism to prevent cases from being prolonged and exacerbating existing judicial burdens.
body: Rwanda's Supreme Court President, Domitilla Mukantaganzwa, has cautioned newly appointed judicial officials that incorrect rulings can worsen the country's court backlogs. Speaking after a swearing-in ceremony for seven judges and eight court registrars, Mukantaganzwa emphasized that flawed decisions do not resolve disputes but instead lead to further litigation, thereby increasing the workload on the judiciary.

Mukantaganzwa highlighted that appeals stemming from misjudgments contribute significantly to the existing burden on the courts. She also reminded the officials that professional misconduct, including ethical failures, poor performance, and ignorance, can lead to dismissal from the judiciary, citing past instances of officials being removed for such reasons.

The Supreme Court President urged the new officials to uphold high standards, warning them against corruption and nepotism to ensure the genuine administration of justice. She stressed the importance of receiving citizens with humility and professionalism, advising against situations where individuals arrive at court early and leave without assistance.

Mukantaganzwa also called for timely attention and professional treatment for all who interact with the courts, stating that access to justice requires decisions that resolve disputes rather than prolong them. She particularly emphasized the critical role of primary courts, which form the foundation of the justice system, and the need for good service at this level.

Furthermore, Mukantaganzwa encouraged teamwork and consultation among the newly appointed officials and their experienced colleagues, stressing that judicial work requires collective responsibility. She urged all 15 new officials, including primary court presidents, primary court judges, and court registrars, to remain faithful to their oaths and to ensure justice is both administered and visibly seen in their actions and public service.

Soji-George Consulting Nigeria Limited and the Lagos State Ministry of Establishments and Training. This partnership resulted in an AI, Governance and Economic Transformation (AI-GET) Executive Leadership Masterclass designed for senior public officials.
articles.takeaway: The University of Kigali partnered with Nigerian entities to offer an executive leadership masterclass focused on artificial intelligence, governance, and economic transformation for senior public officials.
body: The University of Kigali (UoK) has extended its executive education programs to Nigeria, collaborating with J. Soji-George Consulting Nigeria Limited and the Lagos State Ministry of Establishments and Training. This partnership resulted in an AI, Governance and Economic Transformation (AI-GET) Executive Leadership Masterclass designed for senior public officials.

The two-day program, held in Lagos, aimed to explore how artificial intelligence, transformational leadership, and responsible innovation can enhance governance, institutional performance, and public service delivery. The initiative underscores UoK's commitment to fostering African-led solutions for leadership and development challenges.

Participants focused on aligning leadership, policy, institutional capacity, data, and accountability to achieve meaningful transformation, rather than solely on technology. Key areas covered included AI literacy, emotional intelligence, transformational leadership, economic transformation, and responsible AI governance, encompassing data protection, transparency, and accountability.

The masterclass incorporated a practical approach, encouraging participants to identify service delivery challenges within their agencies and consider how emerging technologies and effective leadership could address them. Rwanda's experience with results-oriented governance and performance contracting, as well as the Zipline Rwanda case study on healthcare delivery, were used to illustrate practical knowledge exchange and successful implementation strategies.

This initiative highlights the growing role of African universities in cross-border executive education and public-sector capacity development. It emphasizes that successful digital transformation relies on capable institutions, effective partnerships, responsible governance, and sustained execution, in addition to innovative technologies.

articles.dek: Rwanda will host a Formula 1 race from the early 2030s under a 10-year agreement that will bring the championship back to Africa for the first time since 1993. The African Grand Prix will take place at a purpose-built c…
articles.lead: Rwanda will host a Formula 1 race from the early 2030s under a 10-year agreement that will bring the championship back to Africa for the first time since 1993. The African Grand Prix will take place at a purpose-built circuit in Bugesera, southeast of Kigali, near the new international airport.
articles.takeaway: Rwanda will host a Formula 1 race from the early 2030s under a 10-year agreement that will bring the championship back to Africa for the first time since 1993.
body: Rwanda will host a Formula 1 race from the early 2030s under a 10-year agreement that will bring the championship back to Africa for the first time since 1993. The African Grand Prix will take place at a purpose-built circuit in Bugesera, southeast of Kigali, near the new international airport.

Formula 1 said the track will be built to FIA Grade 1 standards and is expected to be ready early in the next decade. The deal makes Rwanda the first confirmed new Formula 1 host country since Saudi Arabia and Qatar joined the calendar in 2021.

It also gives the championship a race on every inhabited continent. Rwanda President Paul Kagame said the event is intended to support tourism, investment, jobs and skills development rather than serve as a single race weekend.

The wider Bugesera project will include sports, tourism, infrastructure and commercial development around the circuit. Formula 1 has been absent from Africa since the 1993 South African Grand Prix at Kyalami.

South Africa had been seen as the main candidate for a return, while Morocco has also explored hosting a race. Rwanda began a formal push for a Grand Prix in 2024 and has since worked with Formula 1 and the FIA on the project.
Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton has also called for the series to return to the continent. The agreement extends Rwanda's use of global sport as part of its tourism and investment strategy.

articles.headline: Teen Challenge Rwanda Helps Man Recover from Addiction and Leg Injury
articles.dek: A young man shares his journey of overcoming drug addiction and a debilitating leg injury with the help of Teen Challenge Rwanda and Comfort My People Ministry.
articles.lead: Manirahari Ulliel, originally from Musanze, has expressed gratitude to Teen Challenge Rwanda and Comfort My People Ministry for their role in his recovery. The organizations not only treated a severe leg wound that had plagued him but also helped him overcome drug and alcohol addiction, leading him to embrace Christianity.
articles.takeaway: A young man shares his journey of overcoming drug addiction and a debilitating leg injury with the help of Teen Challenge Rwanda and Comfort My People Ministry.
body: Manirahari Ulliel, originally from Musanze, has expressed gratitude to Teen Challenge Rwanda and Comfort My People Ministry for their role in his recovery. The organizations not only treated a severe leg wound that had plagued him but also helped him overcome drug and alcohol addiction, leading him to embrace Christianity.

Manirahari recounted his struggles, which began with a leg injury that went untreated, leading to an open wound and subsequent reliance on marijuana and alcohol. He found himself on the streets of Nyabugogo, feeling hopeless. His life changed when he encountered a pastor who brought him and four other young men to the Teen Challenge center in Kamonyi.

His leg condition, initially suspected to be witchcraft, caused swelling in his legs and arms. Despite seeking traditional healing and medical attention, the wound persisted. Life on the streets was harsh, marked by lack of shelter, food, and frequent beatings, along with run-ins with security forces.

Upon arriving at Teen Challenge, Manirahari was initially resistant to the spiritual guidance offered. However, the center's staff continued to counsel him and assured him that his leg wound would be treated. After accepting Jesus Christ, he found a new purpose, viewing his body as a temple and dedicating himself to following Christ's path.

Teen Challenge provided Manirahari with vocational training, including soap making, and taught him English. He is now focused on building a positive future and advises other young people to distance themselves from negative influences. His mother, Mukasine Christine, confirmed the severity of his leg condition, which led to his addiction and eventual disappearance from home. She expressed immense relief and gratitude upon seeing his recovery.

Manirahari received treatment at ADEPR Nyamata Hospital, facilitated by Comfort My People Ministry through Teen Challenge Rwanda, with care from the Rwanda Military Hospital in Nyamata. Bishop François Kamana, head of Teen Challenge Rwanda, stated that the organization aims to rehabilitate youth facing various challenges, including lack of civic education and moral values, to build a stronger future for Rwanda. The center has assisted over 200 individuals from various countries and seeks government support to expand its reach.

attribution.originalTitle: Baramvuye ndakira, bamvanye mu biyobyabwenge, bamenyesha Yesu - Manirahari ashimira Teen Challenge

faqs.question: What services does Teen Challenge Rwanda provide?
faqs.answer: Teen Challenge Rwanda offers rehabilitation from drug addiction, vocational training, spiritual guidance, and educational support to young people facing various life challenges.

faqs.question: How long did Manirahari struggle with his leg injury and addiction?
faqs.answer: Manirahari had suffered from his leg injury for five years and spent a year on the streets before being admitted to Teen Challenge Rwanda.

articles.lead: The Rwandan government has offered support to traders and the private sector following a significant fire at GOICO Plaza, the main market in Musanze District. The blaze, which occurred on Saturday, October 10, caused no fatalities but resulted in minor injuries for two individuals, with 15 others treated for psychological shock. Two people remain hospitalized.
articles.takeaway: A fire at GOICO Plaza, the largest market in Rwanda's Northern Province, caused no fatalities but injured two people and left 15 others in shock.
body: The Rwandan government has offered support to traders and the private sector following a significant fire at GOICO Plaza, the main market in Musanze District. The blaze, which occurred on Saturday, October 10, caused no fatalities but resulted in minor injuries for two individuals, with 15 others treated for psychological shock. Two people remain hospitalized.

The fire started on the rooftop of the five-storey building around 4:00 PM and quickly spread, affecting large quantities of goods across multiple floors. Firefighting efforts continued until Sunday morning.

The Ministry of Local Government issued a statement expressing solidarity with those affected and commending the swift response from the Rwanda National Police Fire and Rescue Brigade, local authorities, and residents, which prevented the fire from spreading to adjacent structures.

An investigation is underway to determine the cause of the fire. The government has committed to assisting in the rehabilitation of the market to enable businesses to resume operations. GOICO Plaza is a major hub for approximately 2,000 traders, making it the largest market building in the Northern Province. The full extent of the financial damage is still under assessment.

articles.headline: Rwanda and Kenya Deepen Ties with 11 New Agreements
articles.dek: Nairobi meeting yields pacts on legal assistance, immigration, and urban development, alongside growing trade and energy cooperation.
articles.lead: Rwanda and Kenya have solidified their bilateral relationship by signing 11 new Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) during the 10th Session of the Kenya-Rwanda Joint Permanent Commission for Cooperation (JPCC) in Nairobi. These agreements aim to enhance cooperation across various sectors, including mutual legal assistance in criminal matters, immigration, housing and urban development, and conservation.
articles.takeaway: Nairobi meeting yields pacts on legal assistance, immigration, and urban development, alongside growing trade and energy cooperation.
body: Rwanda and Kenya have solidified their bilateral relationship by signing 11 new Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) during the 10th Session of the Kenya-Rwanda Joint Permanent Commission for Cooperation (JPCC) in Nairobi. These agreements aim to enhance cooperation across various sectors, including mutual legal assistance in criminal matters, immigration, housing and urban development, and conservation.

The expanded cooperation extends beyond formal agreements, with a notable increase in trade, investment, tourism, and the movement of people between the two nations. Trade remains a significant pillar, though Kenya currently holds a substantial lead in goods exchanged. Rwanda imported over $398 million worth of goods from Kenya in 2025, while its exports to Kenya were valued at $5.3 million, highlighting an opportunity for Rwanda to increase its exports.

Transport and logistics are crucial to Rwanda's economy as a landlocked country. Kenya provides vital access to the Port of Mombasa via the Northern Corridor. Formalized through an MOU, a Kenya Ports Authority liaison office in Kigali is intended to streamline cargo coordination. Kenya has also allocated land in Mombasa and Naivashato support Rwandan logistics operations.

Energy security has also been bolstered, with Rwanda receiving its first bulk shipment of refined petroleum products through the Port of Mombasa in September. This arrangement is expected to improve Rwanda's energy security, supply chain efficiency, and reduce logistics costs.

Investment flows are also increasing, with Kenyan financial institutions and businesses having a significant presence in Rwanda. Rwanda has also made investments in Kenyan companies, such as acquiring a stake in the Kenya Pipeline Company, indicating growing reciprocal confidence and a mutual desire to increase two-way investment, particularly in infrastructure and manufacturing.

articles.headline: Rwanda Revises Zoning Rules to Manage Urbanization
articles.dek: New regulations aim to bring clarity and predictability to land use, but successful implementation is crucial for managing rapid urban growth and protecting agricultural land.
articles.lead: Rwanda has introduced revised zoning regulations designed to bring greater order and predictability to its rapidly urbanizing landscape. The updated rules address several key areas, including mixed-use development, building heights, setbacks, parking, industrial activities, and conditional land uses.
articles.takeaway: New regulations aim to bring clarity and predictability to land use, but successful implementation is crucial for managing rapid urban growth and protecting agricultural land.
body: Rwanda has introduced revised zoning regulations designed to bring greater order and predictability to its rapidly urbanizing landscape. The updated rules address several key areas, including mixed-use development, building heights, setbacks, parking, industrial activities, and conditional land uses.

The revisions seek to align national zoning provisions with Kigali's planning framework and district land-use plans. For developers, architects, and landowners, the new regulations are intended to provide clearer guidelines, potentially reducing delays and streamlining the approval process. Some compatible conditional uses have reportedly been reclassified as permitted uses, which could further enhance efficiency.

The regulations also acknowledge the need for essential services within residential zones, allowing for education and health facilities if their scale and location are compatible with the surrounding environment. However, this increased flexibility is balanced with a call for stronger planning discipline.

Authorities are tasked with balancing the need for investment and high-quality housing, such as high-end villas, with the preservation of neighborhood character, infrastructure capacity, and densification goals. The protection of productive agricultural land is highlighted as a priority, with conditional uses in agricultural zones requiring careful consideration to prevent irreversible conversion.

The success of these new zoning regulations hinges on their implementation. Clear public guidance, accessible zoning information, and consistent decision-making across planning authorities are identified as critical factors. Transparency in conditional-use assessments will be important to build confidence among applicants.

attribution.originalTitle: New Zoning Rules Bring Clarity, but Implementation Will Be Key

faqs.question: What are the main goals of Rwanda's revised zoning regulations?
faqs.answer: The revised zoning regulations aim to bring greater order and predictability to land use in Rwanda, particularly in the face of rapid urbanization.

faqs.question: What is considered key to the success of the new zoning rules?
faqs.answer: The consistent and intelligent implementation of the regulations, along with clear public guidance and transparent decision-making, is considered key to their success.

articles.headline: Rwanda and Senegal Sign 11 Cooperation Deals
articles.dek: The agreements aim to strengthen economic ties and expand collaboration across various sectors, following a joint commission meeting.
articles.lead: President Paul Kagame met with Senegal's Minister of African Integration, Foreign Affairs and Senegalese Abroad, Cheikh Niang, on Thursday, October 8. The meeting concluded Niang’s visit to Rwanda, which featured the first session of the Rwanda-Senegal Joint Permanent Commission for Cooperation.
articles.takeaway: The agreements aim to strengthen economic ties and expand collaboration across various sectors, following a joint commission meeting.
body: President Paul Kagame met with Senegal's Minister of African Integration, Foreign Affairs and Senegalese Abroad, Cheikh Niang, on Thursday, October 8. The meeting concluded Niang’s visit to Rwanda, which featured the first session of the Rwanda-Senegal Joint Permanent Commission for Cooperation.

During the commission session, the two countries signed 11 bilateral instruments, including three agreements and eight memoranda of understanding. These cover areas such as political consultations, information and communication technology, tourism, youth, culture, sports, higher education, and scientific research.

The new agreements also address standardization, mutual legal assistance in criminal matters, extradition, and the transfer of sentenced persons, moving cooperation into legal and institutional affairs. Niang conveyed a message of friendship from Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye.

A joint follow-up committee has been established to monitor the implementation of these agreements, with experts set to review progress in 2027. The engagements also included a business forum aimed at increasing trade and investment between the private sectors of both nations.

attribution.originalTitle: Kagame Meets Senegalese Foreign Minister as 11 Cooperation Deals Are Sealed

articles.headline: Rwanda's Economy Sees Agriculture's Share of GDP Decline
articles.dek: While industry and services expand, agriculture's contribution to Rwanda's GDP has fallen, prompting discussions on productivity and farmer livelihoods.
articles.lead: Agriculture now represents approximately one-fifth of Rwanda's economy, a decrease from over a quarter less than a decade ago. Prime Minister Justin Nsengiyumva reported that agriculture's share of gross domestic product (GDP) dropped from 25.6% in 2017 to 20.3% in 2025. During the same period, the industry sector's contribution rose from 17.5% to 22%, and services increased from 48.3% to 52.3%.
articles.takeaway: While industry and services expand, agriculture's contribution to Rwanda's GDP has fallen, prompting discussions on productivity and farmer livelihoods.
body: Agriculture now represents approximately one-fifth of Rwanda's economy, a decrease from over a quarter less than a decade ago. Prime Minister Justin Nsengiyumva reported that agriculture's share of gross domestic product (GDP) dropped from 25.6% in 2017 to 20.3% in 2025. During the same period, the industry sector's contribution rose from 17.5% to 22%, and services increased from 48.3% to 52.3%.

This economic shift aligns with Rwanda's strategy to build a knowledge-based economy driven by industry and value-added exports. However, economists note that the declining share of agriculture raises questions about productivity, farmer incomes, food security, and poverty reduction efforts.

Between 2017 and 2025, Rwanda's GDP grew by an average of 7% annually. Industry experienced an average growth of 8.7%, services 7.9%, and agriculture 4.4% over the same timeframe. Agricultural economist Jules Ngango stated that a shrinking share of GDP for agriculture is not inherently negative, as it can signify the growing importance of other sectors.

Ngango emphasized that the critical factor is whether agriculture itself continues to grow and improve in productivity, even with slower expansion compared to other sectors. He suggested that attention should be directed towards enhancements in agricultural productivity, production, and value addition, alongside monitoring farmers' incomes to ensure improved livelihoods.

Economist Teddy Kaberuka highlighted that agriculture's importance extends beyond its GDP share, given the significant number of Rwandans who depend on it for their livelihoods. He pointed out that weak agricultural performance can impact household incomes and poverty reduction, and that the sector's role as a supplier of raw materials to industries like food processing is crucial.

Kaberuka also noted that while the expansion of services contributes to GDP growth, it is essential to consider who benefits from this growth. He argued that for GDP increases to translate into widespread improvements in living standards, the agriculture sector must continue to develop in parallel with industry and services.

attribution.originalTitle: Agriculture Now a Fifth of Rwanda's GDP - - What Does It Mean?

faqs.question: What is the current share of agriculture in Rwanda's GDP?
faqs.answer: Agriculture currently accounts for about 20.3% of Rwanda's GDP.

faqs.question: What is the average annual growth rate of Rwanda's agriculture sector?
faqs.answer: Between 2017 and 2025, Rwanda's agriculture sector grew at an average annual rate of 4.4%.

articles.takeaway: 4The second Monetary Policy and Financial Stability Statement for 2026 was presented on Thursday.
body: 4The second Monetary Policy and Financial Stability Statement for 2026 was presented on Thursday. KIGALI – The National Bank of Rwanda (BNR) is working with financial institutions to resolve cases in which money sent through the newly launched eKash platform is delayed or fails to reach the intended recipient altogether.

BNR Governor Dr. Soraya Hakuziyaremye said on Thursday that the central bank has moved to address problems that could undermine confidence in digital payments although the rejection rate had fallen below 2% by September.

“Following the full rollout of eKash, there have been some operational issues, as can happen with any new platform deployment,” Hakuziyaremye said following the presentation of BNR’s second Monetary Policy and Financial Stability Statement for 2026.

She concurred that there are still cases where a person sends money and the recipient does not receive it immediately and BNR is now working with both the institution from which a transaction originates and the institution expected to receive it to establish where a delayed payment has stalled and whether it can still be completed.

The intervention is particularly important as digital payments become increasingly embedded in everyday financial transactions, where delays can leave customers uncertain about whether their money has been lost, is still being processed or will eventually reach the intended recipient.
Rwanda’s national digital payment system, eKash, recorded a sharp increase in usage, with active accounts rising from 2.03 million in September 2025 to 10.3 million in September 2026.

articles.headline: NCBA Bank Rwanda Offers 105% Mortgage for Masaka Housing Project
articles.dek: A $22 million housing development in Kigali's Masaka neighborhood is nearing completion, with NCBA Bank Rwanda providing a mortgage product to facilitate homeownership.
articles.lead: A $22 million housing development, Masaka Views Eco Estate, located in Masaka, Kigali, has reached 85% completion. The project, developed by US company Fortis Green Housing, will feature 382 housing units, including apartments, detached houses, and townhouses.
articles.takeaway: A $22 million housing development in Kigali's Masaka neighborhood is nearing completion, with NCBA Bank Rwanda providing a mortgage product to facilitate homeownership.
body: A $22 million housing development, Masaka Views Eco Estate, located in Masaka, Kigali, has reached 85% completion. The project, developed by US company Fortis Green Housing, will feature 382 housing units, including apartments, detached houses, and townhouses.

NCBA Bank Rwanda has partnered with Fortis Green Housing to offer prospective buyers a 105% mortgage product called Tura Neza. This financing option is designed to cover the costs associated with purchasing a home, including insurance.

Prospective buyers are invited to visit the construction site to view the available properties. Homes for sale range in price from Rwf102 million to Rwf212 million, with units including two-bedroom and four-bedroom houses.

The Masaka Views Eco Estate is part of Kigali's broader efforts to expand housing options and improve urban living conditions. The development aims to provide a mix of homes for sale and rent in the growing Masaka area.

attribution.originalTitle: NCBA Bank Rwanda Offers 105% Mortgage for $22 Million Housing Project in Masaka

faqs.answer: The Masaka Views Eco Estate development is 85% complete and includes plans for 382 housing units.

faqs.answer: NCBA Bank Rwanda offers a 105% mortgage product, Tura Neza, to help buyers finance their home purchases in the Masaka Views Eco Estate.
